messages:
ashley: Heads-up: we just got a p95/p99 alert for Hosted API in us-west. P95 jumped from 210ms -> 1.3s and p99 to ~3.6s over a 4m window. Not all tenants affected. :warning:

sre-bot: Alert: hosted-api-us-west latency_p95 > 1000ms (1809876520). Trace id: t-8c3f.

miguel: On it. Can someone post queue depth + scheduler logs for the window? Thinking noisy-tenant or kernel fallback.

kai: I pulled runtime traces for 1809876500-1809876560. Key observations: increased queue depth on a subset of backends, a spike in kernel selection fallbacks (optimized -> generic) at 1809876518, and KV cache miss rate doubled for a hot prefix.

lara: Incoming: customer A had a sudden burst around the same time (500 requests/s for ~30s) — could be the noisy neighbor. They were on shared pool.

ashley: Is the rate limiter bounded per-tenant? Could a burst push other tenants into deeper queues?

miguel: Rate limiter is token-bucket per-API-key; but shared worker threads and batch slots are global per-pool. A tenant can saturate batch formation and force smaller batches, which increases per-token overhead.

kai: Paste from profiler (simplified):
```
1809876516: batch_size histogram: 1-2: 42%, 3-8: 48%, 9+: 10%
1809876518: kernel path: optimized_kernel chosen 22% -> generic_kernel 78% (fallback due to seq_len mismatch)
1809876520: kv_cache miss_rate: 0.12 -> 0.36 for prefix "ctx:session:abc"
cpu: threads idle% dropped 25%->3%
```

ops-bot: Deploybot: no deploys during incident window.

ashley: So two amplifying factors: kernel fallback causing higher latency per token, and KV cache misses increasing model compute. Any signs of preemption/noisy VM?

kai: Host metrics: one GPU host showed >80% PCIe mem copy stalls briefly; kernel fallback logs correlate — when fallback occurs we do more host<->device movement.

miguel: Proposed immediate mitigation: 1) temporarily pin high QPS tenant to a dedicated burst pool (if available) 2) bump kernel selection heuristic to prefer optimized_kernel for small seq_len even if not perfectly matched (risk: correctness/perf tradeoff) 3) prime KV cache prefix for affected tenants.

lara: Ops can move tenant to reserved_burst_pool if we decide. Need owner consent.

ashley: Can we run a quick A/B: change batching heuristic to allow forming slightly larger batches for that pool (batch_wait_ms +2) to reduce kernel-switch thrash?

kai: We can toggle batch_wait_ms at runtime per-pool. Suggest 2ms increase for 60s and observe p95. I can also enable KV cache prefetch for prefix scan of top-10 recent keys for tenant.

miguel: I triggered KV prefetch for tenant A at 1809876552 and bumped batch_wait_ms at 1809876558 to +2ms for pool-12. Monitoring now.

(2m later)

kai: Update: after changes p95 dropped to ~260ms and p99 to ~640ms for the pool; kernel fallback rate fell from 78% -> 18%; KV miss rate fell to 0.09. Looks like combo mitigations worked.

ashley: Nice. Next steps: 1) keep temporary settings for 10m while we run root-cause analysis 2) reproduce in staging with a synthetic noisy-tenant workload to validate batching heuristics 3) long-term: add adaptive kernel-preserve mode that tolerates small seq_len deviations to avoid fallback thrash.

miguel: I'll open an action item with perf profile attached and a runbook for per-tenant burst isolation.

lara: I'll reach out to customer A to confirm the burst source and ask if they want dedicated capacity.

ashley: Thanks team. Please add logs/traces to the incident ticket and mark on-call for follow-up. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: Incident resolved (mitigated). Duration: ~7m. Ticket: INC-2026-382.
